title: CmdPal: Late startup can publish an uninstalled extension (EXT26.E4)

judgment.rationale: The issue reports isolated late-notification and completed-task/canceled-token tests. The service event path is tested, but UI/manager non-resurrection still needs verification.
evidence: Isolated tests reproduced late notification after removal and a completed activation task with a canceled token.
The report says the manager's event-time token does not identify the activation lifetime.
StartExtensionWhenReadyAsync creates and publishes a wrapper after awaiting activation; the final registration-lifetime synchronization is the key gap.
judgment.recommended_action: Use the targeted maintainer reproduction to validate the proposed mechanism before design approval; no upstream action has been taken.

fix_assessment.rationale: No matching fix was identified by focused issue-number search; keep the mechanism as a hypothesis pending reproduction.

confidence.rationale: Late notification and cancellation edge are reproduced in isolated tests; synchronization with actual UI publication remains untested.

verification: Hold activation beyond initial timeout, remove provider, release activation and verify no stale event or commands appear.
Repeat with same-ID replacement and ensure old results cannot overwrite or remove it.
Pass completed activation with canceled token and verify cancellation.
plan: Carry the activation's provider-registration lifetime through initialization and publication.
Recheck cancellation/current registration after initialization and synchronize with removal/replacement.
Clean rejected results and handle completed-task/canceled-token cases consistently.
Test uninstall during activation, same-ID replacement and manager/UI non-resurrection.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The delayed-start path initializes and publishes after activation without rechecking original cancellation/registration lifetime; removal or replacement can be followed by obsolete OnProviderAdded.
proposed_fixes.title: Investigate the reported PowerToys behavior
